value: "The Bridge2AI-Voice (B2AI-Voice) dataset is a large, ethically sourced, and demographically diverse voice dataset linked to health information, released by the NIH's Bridge2AI initiative. It was generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium, a Precision Public Health grand challenge project funded by the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program, whose stated goal is a flagship, standardized, and ethically sourced dataset of 10,000 voices linked to health information to fuel research and discovery in voice biomarkers. The dataset couples acoustic recordings of voice, speech, breathing and cough tasks with detailed participant metadata: clinical diagnoses (voice, neurological, mood, respiratory and pediatric voice/speech disorders), validated questionnaires, and demographics. Public releases contain derived representations of the audio (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, articulatory and phonetic features, pitch and loudness measures) rather than the original waveforms; access to raw audio is restricted to a separate controlled-access mechanism. Data are collected at multiple sites across North America. The dataset is distributed as two distinct PhysioNet projects: an adult cohort and a pediatric cohort, described as component resources of this record."

value: "The Bridge2AI-Voice (B2AI-Voice) dataset is a large, ethically sourced, and demographically diverse voice dataset linked to health information, released by the NIH's Bridge2AI initiative. It is produced by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium, a Precision Public Health grand challenge project funded by the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program, whose stated goal is to create a flagship, standardized, ethically sourced dataset of voices linked to health information to fuel research and discovery in voice biomarkers. Data are collected prospectively at multiple sites across North America using a custom smartphone/tablet application (the Bridge2AI-Voice App) for adults and reproschema-ui for pediatric participants, and comprise acoustic tasks (voice, speech, breathing and cough recordings), detailed demographics, confounder surveys, validated patient questionnaires and patient-reported outcomes, and clinically validated diagnoses. Participants are recruited across five disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders - together with controls. The dataset is published as two distinct PhysioNet resources: an adult release (Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information) and a separate pediatric release (Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset). The public releases contain derived audio features (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch, articulatory and phonetic-posteriorgram features) and phenotypic tables rather than raw audio waveforms; raw audio is disseminated only under controlled access to protect participant privacy."
reason: A detailed, coherent human-readable prose description of the dataset, matching the string range and field intent.

value: "Bridge2AI-Voice is an ethically sourced, demographically diverse dataset of voice, speech and respiratory sounds linked to multimodal health information, generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. Participants were recruited at specialty (\"high volume expert\") clinics across five sites in North America on the basis of membership in five predetermined disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders - together with control participants without those conditions. Each participant completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks (sustained phonation, glides, diadochokinesis, breathing and cough sounds, read passages, free speech and cognitive-linguistic tasks), demographic and confounder surveys, and disease-specific validated questionnaires, delivered through a custom tablet application; diagnoses were validated by a qualified clinician against established gold standards or, for the psychiatric cohort, from the electronic health record or an active prescription. The public release is a feature-only (\"AI-ready\") derivation: raw audio waveforms are withheld and the distributed data comprise spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch contours, articulatory (SPARC/EMA) features, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE/Praat static features and audio-quality metrics in Parquet, alongside phenotype and task tables in TSV with JSON data dictionaries. The adult dataset is distributed through PhysioNet; release v3.1.0, published 2026-05-01, covers 833 participants. Raw audio is distributed separately under controlled access via Synapse."
reason: A substantive, human-readable prose description of the dataset; matches string range and the field's purpose.

value: "The Bridge2AI-Voice adult flagship dataset is a large, ethically sourced, demographically diverse collection of voice, speech, and respiratory-sound data linked to health information, generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 adult participants recruited across five sites in North America. Participants were selected on the basis of conditions known to manifest in the voice waveform, spanning five disease cohort categories: voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders, together with control participants without those conditions. Each participant performed a standardized battery of acoustic tasks (breathing, cough, sustained vowel, glides, diadochokinesis, validated read passages, free speech, picture description, story recall, and cognitive-linguistic tasks) and completed demographic, confounder, medical-history, and disease-specific validated questionnaires. Clinical diagnoses were validated by clinicians against established gold standards. The published PhysioNet release contains derived features rather than the original waveforms: spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch contours, articulatory (SPARC/EMA) traces, loudness and periodicity estimates, phonetic posteriorgrams, and static acoustic features from openSMILE, Praat/Parselmouth and torchaudio, alongside per-recording audio-quality metrics, recording metadata, and the full phenotypic tables. Raw audio is disseminated only under a separate controlled-access mechanism via Synapse. The project documentation at docs.b2ai-voice.org additionally describes a separate Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset (300 participants aged 2-18), published as a distinct PhysioNet project rather than a version of this one."
reason: A detailed, informative human-readable prose description of the dataset, matching the string range exactly.

All raw voice data was removed from the public release; the data were extracted from the raw audio to limit re-identification and only extracted features are released. Spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, phonetic posteriorgrams, EMAs and transcriptions from open-response prompts were removed from the feature-only dataset, and spectrograms and similar features were excluded where the audio contained free speech; static features that do not encode the sensitive information were retained. value: "Bridge2AI-Voice is a large, ethically sourced, demographically diverse voice dataset linked to health information, produced by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. It comprises voice, speech, breathing and cough recordings collected with a purpose-built application from participants recruited at North American clinical sites. The project defines five disease cohort categories for which voice changes have been associated with specific diseases: voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders. Participants without those conditions are additionally enrolled as controls. The adult release documented here draws on the four adult disease categories together with controls and was collected at five North American sites; pediatric data are collected under a separate protocol at a pediatric institution and are released as a separate dataset. Recordings are accompanied by detailed demographics, confounder surveys, clinician-validated diagnoses, and validated patient-reported outcome questionnaires. The public PhysioNet release contains data considered low risk, namely derived audio features (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch, articulatory and phonetic posteriorgram features, static acoustic features, and audio quality metrics) rather than the original voice waveforms; raw audio is distributed separately under controlled access. Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 adult participants."
reason: A rich, human-readable prose description of the dataset, matching the string range and the field's intent.
